hero.title: From scattered training to a measured path.
hero.sub: The story of SAMARTH AI: the problem a student team picked, how we built the answer, and who built it.

story.title: Why we built it
story.intro: Smart India Hackathon problem statement SIH26101 comes from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). It asks how India's official statistics staff can keep their skills current, and how training can follow what each person actually needs.
story.timelineLabel: The problem, from scattered training to a measured path

stops.title: Scattered training
stops.body: Officials are expected to keep upskilling. The iGOT Karmayogi catalogue is large, but it does not say which courses fit a given role.

stops.title: Gaps nobody measures
stops.body: There is no intelligent skill-gap assessment for official statistics, so courses get chosen by habit or availability, not by measured need.

stops.title: Assessments take too long
stops.body: Trainers lack a fast way to create assessments, so checking what people know stays rare and slow.

stops.title: No view of the workforce
stops.body: Administrators cannot see competencies across a whole workforce, so training plans stay guesswork.

stops.title: A measured path
stops.body: SAMARTH AI is our answer: measure each competency, compare it with what the role needs, and recommend learning that closes the biggest gaps.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.statement: Every official in the statistical system should be able to see where their skills stand, what to learn next and how far they have come, and every institution should be able to see the same, securely and fairly.

how.title: How we built it
how.intro: Five chapters, from the first idea to what comes next. Chapters marked in progress or planned are not finished.

chapters.title: Start from the brief
chapters.body: We read problem statement SIH26101 and turned it into one goal: help every official see their skills, close their gaps and keep learning. Then we wrote down who uses the product: learners, trainers, administrators and platform administrators.
points: A prototype, not an official site

chapters.title: A framework to measure against
chapters.body: Skills need a shared scale. The competency framework has 4 domains, 43 competencies and 6 proficiency levels from 0 to 5, and 10 seed roles that say what each job needs. A gap is the required level minus the current level. The framework is written down; loading it into the product is still in progress.

chapters.title: A backend you can trust
chapters.body: An Express and MongoDB API. Milestone 1 is built: accounts, sessions, uploads and a hash-chained audit trail. The learning features come next.
points: HttpOnly cookie sessions with CSRF checks
Role checks on every protected route

chapters.title: An interface for everyone
chapters.body: React with shadcn components and one set of colour tokens for light and dark themes. The marketing site and account screens are built; the dashboards are placeholders for now.

chapters.title: What comes next
chapters.body: A mock iGOT adapter, competency profiles and gap analysis, AI-drafted quizzes that trainers review, recommendations with reasons, and dashboards. All of this is planned and none of it is finished.

ladder.title: The proficiency ladder
ladder.intro: Every competency is rated on six levels, from 0 to 5.

levels.name: None
levels.summary: No exposure to the competency yet.

levels.name: Awareness
levels.summary: Knows the terms and the purpose, and needs guidance.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.summary: Handles complex cases and guides others.

items.title: Explainable
items.body: Every recommendation and question shows its reason or source.

items.title: Numbers by code, language by AI
items.body: Levels and gaps come from tested formulas. AI drafts, extracts and ranks inside validated limits.

items.title: People decide
items.body: Trainers approve questions. Administrators can override.

items.title: Privacy by design
items.body: Minimum data, and no personal data sent to the AI model.

items.title: Honest about limits
items.body: We label what is simulated or planned.

items.title: Accessible and bilingual
items.body: Keyboard friendly, WCAG 2.2 AA target, English and Hindi.

roadmap.title: Project timeline
roadmap.intro: Weeks are counted from project kickoff. Calendar dates are still to be set by the team.

phases.title: Setup
phases.body: Stack running, contracts agreed, framework draft.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.body: Login and roles, profile, framework, iGOT mock, UI shell.

phases.title: Core AI
phases.body: Gap analysis, recommendations, content pipeline, quiz generation with review.

phases.title: Loop closure and dashboards
phases.body: Quiz attempts, evidence to score to recommendation, admin analytics, tutor.

phases.title: Security and polish
phases.body: Audit chain, anchoring, mock SSO, Hindi, labs, hardening.

phases.title: Test, deploy, present
phases.body: Stable demo URL, evaluation numbers, rehearsals.

tech.title: Technology
tech.intro: Modular, adapter-based architecture: the AI model, iGOT, email, storage and ledger sit behind swappable adapters.

developers.title: The developers
developers.intro: Six people built SAMARTH AI. Each card says what they built.
developers.placeholderNote: Names, roles, notes, photos and links are placeholders. The team will replace them before launch.

disclaimer.title: Prototype disclaimer
disclaimer.body: SAMARTH AI is a student prototype built in response to Smart India Hackathon problem statement SIH26101 (MoSPI). It is not an official Government of India website or service, and it is not endorsed by or affiliated with MoSPI, NSSTA, iGOT Karmayogi or the Government of India. Courses, integrations and some figures are simulated for demonstration.
